---
title: The configuration
description: The options in _smalldocs.yml that smalldocs reads, and how it reads a _quarto.yml.
order: 2
---

The config file of a project is `_smalldocs.yml`, in the folder of the project. smalldocs can also read
`_quarto.yml`, the config file of Quarto. See [A _quarto.yml](#a-_quarto.yml) below.

```yaml
project:
  type: website
website:
  title: My project
theme: cosmo         # the options of each page are at the top level
toc: true
linkify: true        # the options of smalldocs are at the top level too; see Linkify below
api:
  packages: [mypkg]
```

An option is a key in `_smalldocs.yml`, in a `_metadata.yml` file or in the front matter of a page.
smalldocs merges the options in this order, and a later value wins:

1. The top level of `_smalldocs.yml`.
2. A `_metadata.yml` file in each folder on the path to the page. smalldocs does not read a
   `_metadata.yml` in the folder of the project. Put those options in `_smalldocs.yml`.
3. The front matter of the page.

`metadata-files` is a list of more YAML files, with paths from the folder of the project. smalldocs
merges them into `_smalldocs.yml`, and a key in `_smalldocs.yml` wins over the same key in these files.

If smalldocs does not read an option, the build gives a warning. With `smalldocs render --strict`, a
warning makes the build fail.

Each table below gives the default of each option, which is what smalldocs does when you do not set it.
The smallest config is a `_smalldocs.yml` with no keys. Then smalldocs builds every page in the
folder with the theme `cosmo`, and with no navbar, sidebar or table of contents.

## project

| Key | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `type` | `website`, or `default`, which is the same. `book`, a type of project in Quarto, is built as a website, with its chapters as the sidebar. Another type stops the build | `website` |
| `output-dir` | The output folder. See the note below the table | `_site` |
| `render` | One glob, or a list of globs, of the pages to build. A glob is a path pattern; see [Globs](#globs). A glob that starts with `!` leaves pages out | Every `.qmd`, `.md` and `.ipynb` file, except the files that are left out below |
| `resources` | One glob, or a list of globs, of more files to copy into the site, such as `.nojekyll` or `images/**` | None. A file that a page links to, such as an image, is copied without this option |
| `pre-render`, `post-render` | Commands to run before and after the build, in the folder of the project. A command that is one `.py` file runs with the Python of smalldocs. See the note below the table | None |

A command of `pre-render` or `post-render` gets these environment variables. Their names come from
Quarto, so a script written for Quarto still works:

- `QUARTO_PROJECT_DIR`: the folder of the project
- `QUARTO_PROJECT_OUTPUT_DIR`: the output folder, from the folder of the project
- `QUARTO_PROJECT_INPUT_FILES` and `QUARTO_PROJECT_OUTPUT_FILES`: the pages and the files that the build
  writes, one on each line, as paths from the folder of the project
- `QUARTO_PROJECT_RENDER_ALL`: `1`, because each build makes every page
- `SMALLDOCS`: `1`, so a script can tell smalldocs from Quarto

Each build deletes the old content of the output folder. So smalldocs refuses an output folder in these
cases:

- The folder is the project, or a folder above the project.
- The folder holds a `.git` folder.
- The folder holds files, but no `site_libs` folder. A `site_libs` folder shows that an earlier build
  made the folder.

Without `render`, smalldocs leaves out these files:

- the files and folders whose names start with `_` or `.`
- the output folder
- the folders `env`, `venv`, `renv`, `node_modules`, `site-packages` and `__pycache__`
- each file with the name `README`, such as `README.md` or `readme.qmd`

To build a page that one of these rules leaves out, list it in `render`.

## Globs

A glob is a path pattern, such as `guide/*.qmd`. smalldocs reads globs by these rules, which are the
rules of Quarto:

- In a glob with a `/`, the `*` stays inside one folder, and `**` crosses folders. So `guide/*` finds
  `guide/a.qmd`, but not `guide/old/b.qmd`. `guide/**` finds both.
- A glob with no `/`, such as `*.qmd`, finds files in every folder.
- A folder name, such as `guide/`, means the pages in the folder.

Sometimes a page links to a page that is not built, for example a draft. smalldocs reports the link,
and it never copies the source of that page into the site.

## website

| Key | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `title` | The name of the site, in the navbar and in the browser tab after the title of the page | None. The browser tab shows only the title of the page |
| `description` | The summary of the site. The home page uses it when its front matter has no `description` | None |
| `site-url` | The address of the site. smalldocs needs it for `sitemap.xml` and for feeds | None, and smalldocs writes no `sitemap.xml` |
| `repo-url`, `repo-subdir` | The repository of the site, and the folder of the site in it | None |
| `repo-branch` | The branch for the `edit` and `source` links | `main` |
| `repo-actions` | Links under the table of contents: `edit`, `source`, `issue`. They need `repo-url` | None |
| `navbar` | `left`, `right`, `tools`, `title`, `logo`, `background`, `search`. An entry is a page, or `href` and `text`, with an `icon`. `menu` makes a dropdown | No navbar. The sidebar then shows the title of the site |
| `sidebar` | `contents`, `style`, `title`, `logo`, `search`, `tools`, `collapse-level`. A list gives several sidebars | No sidebar |
| `sidebar.style` | `floating` sits beside the text, and `docked` is a full-height panel at the left edge | `floating` |
| `sidebar.collapse-level` | The sections above this level start open. With `2`, the top-level sections start open, and the sections inside them start closed. A section that holds the current page is always open | `2` |
| `page-navigation` | Links to the previous page and the next page of the sidebar | Off |
| `page-footer` | One text, or `left`, `center` and `right`. Each part is Markdown or a list of entries | None |
| `search` | The search box. `false` turns search off | On |
| `favicon` | The icon in the browser tab | None |
| `open-graph` | The Open Graph tags, which give the title and the picture that a link to the page shows in other apps | Off |
| `bread-crumbs` | The breadcrumbs, the path of the page above its title. `false` hides them | On |

The `contents` of a sidebar takes these entries:

```yaml
sidebar:
  contents:
    - index.qmd                      # a page
    - section: Guide                 # a section that folds
      contents: guide/*              # a glob: by `order:`, then the index page, then by path
    - section: Reference
      href: api/index.qmd            # a section that is also a page
      contents:
        - api/one.qmd
    - auto: examples                 # one section for each folder, titled by its index page
    - text: Elsewhere
      href: https://example.com
    - text: "---"                    # a line
```

## The options of a page

Write these options at the top level of `_smalldocs.yml` or of a `_metadata.yml` file. A page can also
set them in its front matter. smalldocs reads `theme` only from the config of the
project. It reads `order` only from the front matter of a page.

| Key | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `theme` | A Bootswatch name, a CSS file, an extension in `_extensions/`, or `light:` and `dark:` for two themes and a toggle. See [Themes](themes.qmd) | `cosmo` |
| `css` | Your stylesheets, after the stylesheet of the theme | None |
| `toc` | The table of contents at the right of the page | Off |
| `toc-depth` | The deepest level of heading in the table of contents | `3` |
| `toc-title` | The heading above the table of contents | `On this page` |
| `number-sections` | Numbers before the headings | Off |
| `code-copy` | The copy button on code | On |
| `from` | Turns off a part of the Markdown. `markdown-smart` keeps quotes and dashes as you type them. `markdown-tex_math_dollars` reads each `$` as a dollar. `markdown-smart-tex_math_dollars` does both | `markdown`, with every part on |
| `page-layout` | `article`, `full` or `custom` | `article` |
| `link-external-newwindow` | Open links to other sites in a new tab | Off |
| `include-in-header`, `include-before-body`, `include-after-body` | Files, or `text:` entries, to put into each page | None |
| `echo`, `output`, `include`, `execute` | `false` hides the code or the output of every cell, in a notebook or in a page. `execute: {echo: false}` works too | `true`: the code and the output show |
| `title` | The title of the page | A level-one heading (`#`) at the very top of the page. Otherwise the name of the file, with a space for each `-` and `_` |
| `subtitle`, `description`, `author`, `date`, `categories`, `image` | The title block, which is the title, subtitle, author and date at the top of the page. Also what a [listing](listings.qmd) shows | None |
| `date-format` | How the title block writes `date`, such as `YYYY-MM-DD`, `long` or `short` | `MMMM D, YYYY`, such as `October 12, 2026` |
| `draft` | `true` leaves the page out of the site | `false` |
| `order` | The place of a page among the pages that a glob of the sidebar finds. A listing has its own `sort` | None. The page comes after the pages that have an `order` |
| `listing` | A list of other pages. See [Listings](listings.qmd) | None |
| `title-block-banner` | A band of the primary colour behind the title | Off |

## The options of smalldocs

These options belong to smalldocs. They are at the top level of `_smalldocs.yml`.

| Key | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `linkify` | A documented name in backticks links to its entry in the API reference. See [Linkify](#linkify) | On when `api` has `packages`, or when the `filters` of a `_quarto.yml` name `linkify.lua`. Off otherwise |
| `symbols` | The index of names that linkify reads, from the folder of the site. Set it only for an index that you write yourself, without `api`. The `api` section always writes `_symbols.json` | `_symbols.json` |
| `api` | The API reference. See [The API reference](api.qmd#turn-on-the-reference) | None: no reference |

## Linkify

Linkify turns a name in backticks into a link to the entry of that name in the API reference. For
example, `` `Site.build` `` and `` `Site.build()` `` link to the entry of `Site.build`. Linkify links
only names that look like code, such as a call, a dotted name or a class. A plain lowercase word, such
as `main`, stays as code. See [Links from the text](api.qmd#links-from-the-text).

Linkify reads the names and their links from the file `_symbols.json`, in the folder of the site. When
the config has `api`, each build writes this file before it builds the pages. See
[The index of names](api.qmd#the-index-of-names).

smalldocs decides whether linkify is on in this order:

1. `linkify`, if you set it. `linkify: true` turns it on, and `linkify: false` turns it off.
2. `api.linkify`, if you set it.
3. Otherwise, linkify is on when `api` has `packages`.

## What a build writes

A build writes the pages, and these files, into the output folder:

- `index.html`, the home page, from `index.qmd`, `index.md` or `index.ipynb` at the top of the folder.
  The title of the site in the navbar links to it. A folder can have an index page too. A link to the
  folder opens it, and an `auto` section of the sidebar takes its title.
- `search.json`, the index of the search box. It has one entry for each section of each page, with the
  title of the section and its text. A page with `search: false` in its front matter is not in it.
- `sitemap.xml`, the list of pages for search engines, when `site-url` is set.
- `site_libs`, the stylesheets and the scripts of the site.
- A feed for each listing that asks for one, when `site-url` is set. See [Listings](listings.qmd).
- A copy of each file that a page links to, such as an image, and of the files of `resources`, `css`
  and `favicon`. Each copy keeps its path from the folder of the project.

With an `api` section, a build first writes the reference pages and `_symbols.json` into the folder of
the project. Then it builds them as it builds the other pages. See [The API reference](api.qmd).

## A _quarto.yml

smalldocs looks for `_smalldocs.yml` first. If the folder has no `_smalldocs.yml`, smalldocs reads
`_quarto.yml`. If the folder has both files, smalldocs reads only `_smalldocs.yml`, and gives a warning.

A `_quarto.yml` has the same `project` and `website` sections. Two parts are in other places:

- The options of a page are under `format.html`.
- The options of smalldocs are under `smalldocs:`. Quarto ignores a top-level key that it does not
  know, so Quarto can still build the project.

```yaml
format:
  html:
    theme: cosmo
    toc: true
smalldocs:
  linkify: true
  api:
    packages: [mypkg]
```

Under `smalldocs:`, `theme` names the theme that smalldocs uses, in place of `format.html.theme`. So
Quarto can compile its Sass theme, and smalldocs can use the CSS of the same extension.

smalldocs also reads a custom format of an extension, such as `format: tufte-html`, as `html`. See
[Themes](themes.qmd).

To move to `_smalldocs.yml`, rename the file. Move the keys of `format.html` and of `smalldocs:` to the
top level. Then remove `format` and `filters`. If you write `format`, `smalldocs` or `filters` in
`_smalldocs.yml`, the build gives a warning and does not read the key.

### Lua filters

smalldocs runs no Lua. Its linkify is Python code, and it does the work of the Lua filter
`linkify.lua`, with one difference. The filter links every name in the index. smalldocs links only
names that look like code, so a plain lowercase word, such as `encode`, stays as code. Write it as a
call, `encode()`, to link it.

In a `_quarto.yml`, a file with the name `linkify.lua` in `filters` also turns on linkify, as step 3
of the list above. smalldocs does not read the file `linkify.lua`, and does not run it. The name only
tells smalldocs to turn on linkify. The entry can be a path, such as `filters/linkify.lua`, or
`{path: linkify.lua}`.

smalldocs does not run the other filters in `filters`. It gives a warning for each of them, but not for
the entry `quarto`, which only marks where the filters of Quarto run.
